approach: Add `check_behavior_test_reading` to crates/athena-core/src/reading/surveys.rs, gated by the existing `changes_code_with_behavior_criterion`. Wire it as one `step!` line directly after `step!(check_code_survey(reading))` in checks.rs. Revision 4 changes how each of the four parts is satisfied. (1) Each part is met EITHER by its labelled clause (`Gate order:`, `Existing code:`, `Record kind:`, `Direct check:`) OR by its markers inside a `Code survey:` or `Existing code:` assumption. `check_code_survey`'s own refusal text (surveys.rs:209-214) and `CODE_SURVEY_GUIDE` (reader.rs:356-363) already ask for the entry point, the order of resolution and probing, record validation and the direct measurement in the survey, so past surveys may already hold the content. The check no longer requires labels no past reading used. The error still names each missing part. (2) Negation: a comma directly before `or`/`nor` is one joiner. `and` no longer carries negation, so both `and` forms are refused and pinned. (3) The brief guide sentence is first reworded to fit the 3045-byte baseline, and the bounds are raised only if that fails. (4) An `athena <subcommand>` invocation counts as a direct check for a criterion whose text names that subcommand. `cargo` commands still never count. (5) The error lists the behavior-criterion numbers found and those the `Direct check:` text does not cover. A test inserts a criterion before the referenced one. (6) The fixture replay test is labelled mechanics-only. The bound for AC4 is shown only by `loop_replay` and the verification replay records. The share is still unknown until those run, so the user decision is raised as a blocking open question before dispatch. Parts (a)-(d) otherwise keep the revision-3 design: shared `assumptions_labeled` helper, shared `NEGATORS` constant, closed skip-switch list, command removal, routine-criterion stop list, one error naming all missing parts and the check. status.rs, verify.rs and replay.rs stay unchanged and are listed in `unchanged_planned_files`. No prompt file, record, athena.toml, defaults.toml or workflow is touched.

decisions.choice: Each part (a)-(d) is satisfied by its labelled clause OR by markers in any `Code survey:` or `Existing code:` assumption; the error names every part neither route satisfies. Markers: (a) one assumption holding at least two broad identifiers and a stop-gate phrase (`stop gate`, `stops at`, `stops after`, `stop at`, `stops before`). (b) an `Existing code:` assumption with a crates/ path the job does not create and a broad identifier, or a `Code survey:` holding `reuse`, `reuses`, `reused` or `reusing` plus a broad identifier. (c) a `Record kind:` clause, or a `Code survey:` that satisfies `names_record_evidence`, or a `Code survey:` holding `no record` or `adds no record`. (d) a `Direct check:` body naming the criteria, or a `Code survey:` holding `measured directly` or `direct check` plus a function-like identifier.
decisions.reason: Finding 1. The replay hold is a Blocker (verify.rs:500-529) above 30+5 points over a 50-reading window (replay.rs:9, 296-308). Requiring three labels no past reading used would newly refuse nearly every code behavior reading. HISTORY.txt shows most of the 50 newest commits change crates/ (for example a5f5700, 334c255, 64b04c9, c9fb473, 31ca8d1), so I estimate 60-80% of recent accepted readings are code or tests readings with a behavior criterion; this is an estimate from commit subjects, not measured, because records/ is absent. Since the survey rule began (2026-10-28) the reader brief has asked for a survey that covers the entry point and order, record validation and direct measurement, so some past surveys may already carry the markers. The marker route lowers the newly refused share to those readings whose surveys lack the content. How far it falls is unknown until `loop_replay` runs. The labels stay as the explicit, best-matched route and let the error name a missing part. The plan does not claim the share is under 35%.

rejected.why: Every code behavior reading is newly refused; the hold almost certainly fires.
The error could then not tell the reader what to write; labels give a precise fix and a precise test for the missing part.

rejected.option: Loosen markers until the share is under 35%
rejected.why: AC4 forbids loosening markers to fit the share; the markers are fixed before the run and the measured share is reported.

decisions.choice: Part (b) by label: an `Existing code:` assumption found with `existing_code_assumptions` (surveys.rs:1329-1336) that names a crates/ path the job does not create (`names_existing_path`, surveys.rs:1341) and one broad identifier. A new generic `assumptions_labeled(reading, label)` helper replaces the three copies of the label filter (surveys.rs:117-124, 605-612, 1329-1336).
decisions.reason: `check_design_existing_code` already uses that label for reuse, so a reading that states reuse the usual way is not refused; fewer new labels means a smaller newly refused share. One helper keeps the three filters in step.

rejected.why: No past reading used it; it adds to the newly refused share.

decisions.choice: Part (a) clause `Gate order:`: a body with at least two broad identifiers and a stop-gate phrase. A broad identifier is a token with `_` or `::`, a word directly followed by `()`, or a backticked single token; a token with `/` or a file extension never counts. Part (c): a `Record kind:` body that satisfies `names_record_evidence`, or is `none` while no deliverable satisfies `is_record_or_data_deliverable`. `Record kind: none` beside a record or data deliverable is refused as a contradiction naming (c) and the file. The new check does not re-test survey evidence; `check_code_survey` (surveys.rs:217-230) runs first and refuses a record deliverable whose survey lacks evidence. The contradiction fixtures carry a survey naming `check_record_file`, so the new check is the refuser there.
decisions.reason: Round 3 finding 1. A round-trip-deliverable-path branch could never decide the outcome, because a record deliverable never reaches this check without survey evidence. AC3's 'no accepted record kind and no round-trip test deliverable' is refused in two places by design: `check_code_survey` when the survey has no evidence (a corpus case pins it) and the new check when `Record kind: none` meets a record file. Backticked single words such as `replay` (replay.rs:365) stay valid entry points.

rejected.why: Dead branch.

rejected.option: Re-check record evidence from the survey in the new check
rejected.why: Duplicates check_code_survey.
AC3 requires the contradiction to be refused.

rejected.option: Count only tokens with `_` or `::` in (a)
rejected.why: A single-word entry point would never count.

decisions.choice: Part (d). Each non-routine behavior criterion must be covered. With the label, the number of each such criterion appears in a `Direct check:` body, found by `criterion_numbers` (forms `criterion N`, `criteria N-M`, and lists `criteria N, M and K`, with `or`, `&` and commas) on lowercase text. The body holds a function-like identifier (`_`, `::` or `name()`). Before scanning, strip backtick spans starting `cargo ` and the word `cargo` to the end of its clause; a `cargo` command never counts. A backtick span starting `athena <subcommand>` is kept and counts as a direct check only for a criterion whose text contains that subcommand word, for example `athena check-reading` for a criterion about what `check-reading` prints. Any other `athena ` span is removed. Via the survey marker route (d) is met for all criteria at once. The error lists the behavior-criterion numbers found, the numbers a `Direct check:` text covers, and those missing, so a stale reference is obvious. Skip switches: the closed list `skip_probe`, `ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, and upper-case tokens starting `ATHENA_NO_` or `ATHENA_SKIP_` (case-sensitive); lower-case names that merely contain `skip_` never match, so `skip_note` (checks.rs:271) is accepted. Internal-helper phrases: `internal helper`, `private helper`, `stand-in`, `through a helper`, `via a helper`. A non-negated match refuses. The scan covers the `Direct check:` bodies and, on the survey route, the survey sentence holding the marker (split at `. ` or `;`).
decisions.reason: Findings 4 and 5 and earlier rounds. For a criterion about CLI output (this request's criterion 5) running the binary is the direct observation, so refusing it would push readers toward helper-level checks; `cargo test` runs measure nothing about the property and stay refused. Numbers can go stale when the user edits criteria, so the error shows found, covered and missing numbers. The reading checks read the Reading only (surveys.rs:310-311), so the switch list cannot be checked against code and is closed and stated as a limit.

rejected.why: Finding 4: refuses an honest direct check for CLI-output criteria.

rejected.option: Accept any command as a direct check
rejected.why: `cargo test -p x` measures nothing about the property.
Refuses `skip_note`.

rejected.option: Leave a stale number silently refused
rejected.why: Finding 5: the reader cannot tell which number is missing.

decisions.choice: Negation (finding 2). One shared `pub(super) const NEGATORS: [&str; 7]` (`no`, `not`, `never`, `without`, `nothing`, `nor`, `cannot`), with the existing `n't` and `n\u{2019}t` normalisation, replaces the local list in `requires_existing_code_section` (surveys.rs:1359-1394) and is used by the new check. `rather than` counts; a bare `than` does not. For a match at token i, walk back over determiners and modifiers (`a`, `an`, `the`, `any`, `internal`, `private`, `helper`), at most one connective (`through`, `via`, `using`, `with`, `by`, `of`), and determiners again, and read token j. A negator at j negates. If j is `or` or `nor`, treating a single `,` directly before it as part of the same joiner, and the token before the joiner (skipping determiners) is itself a match, return `negated` of that earlier match. `and` is not a joiner and a bare `,` does not carry negation. Accepted by test: `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `without skip_probe, or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `not through skip_probe nor ATHENA_NO_PROBE`, `no skip_probe, no helper stand-in`, `not through a helper`, `without ATHENA_NO_PROBE`. Refused by test and pinned under Limits: `no probe runs when skip_probe is set`, `faster than skip_probe`, `not through skip_probe and ATHENA_NO_PROBE is set`, `not through skip_probe, and ATHENA_NO_PROBE is set`, `without skip_probe and ATHENA_NO_PROBE` (the writer must repeat `without` or use `or`), `without skip_probe, ATHENA_NO_PROBE`.
decisions.reason: Both `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE` and its comma form are ordinary negated mentions AC3 says to accept. Dropping `and` and bare `,` as carriers makes the comma and no-comma forms behave the same and keeps the later switch in the refused cases visible. verify.rs:1261 holds a clause-level negator for verifier claims; it works on different text and stays unchanged.

rejected.why: Accepts the no-comma form of a case the plan means to refuse.
Refuses `without skip_probe or ATHENA_NO_PROBE`.
Changes verify.rs; AC8 forbids unrelated changes.

decisions.choice: A criterion is routine, and needs no direct check, when after stripping every whitespace token starting `-` and every token starting `athena-`, the remaining lower-cased alphanumeric words are all in the stop list (cargo, fmt, clippy, test, tests, check, pass, passes, passing, and, the, on, final, tree, still, all, locked, same, as, a, recorded, athena, workspace, warnings, targets, no, unrelated, behavior, changes, change, existing, run) and the criterion holds a pass word and one of fmt, clippy or test(s). Parts (a)-(c) are still required.
decisions.reason: AC3 says a routine criterion needs no direct-check clause. Stripping flags and crate names avoids single-letter stop words for `-D warnings` and `-p`.

rejected.option: Add `d`, `p` and crate names to the stop list
rejected.why: Single letters let unrelated criteria through.

rejected.option: Skip the whole check when all behavior criteria are routine
rejected.why: AC2 still requires (a)-(c).
